Cc: billing@cloudify.io

Subject: Unexplained surge / session-sampling variance on March invoice

Hi Laura,

We reviewed our March invoice and there is a large spike in token usage on 2026-03-31 that doesn’t match our internal request logs. The billed tokens for the day are ~2.1M higher than our own counters.

We suspect this might be related to streaming sessions that were retried on our side — some sessions reconnected but we don't see duplicative requests. Can you provide the detailed per-session token breakdown your metering used (session id, start/end, tokens charged) for the 2026-03-29 — 2026-03-31 window?

We’re holding payment on the outstanding invoice until this is clarified. Please let us know what logs you need from our side and whether Redwood can pause the collection while we reconcile.

Thanks,
Emma Chen
Head of Finance, Cloudify
[Cloudify Billing: billing@cloudify.io]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: INF-8421: initial triage — session-sampling edge case (internal)

Laura / Rishi — I pulled the usage export for Cloudify for 03/29–03/31 and ran our token reconciliation tool against their sample. Preliminary notes:

- We see a pattern where streaming sessions that were retried due to client disconnects resulted in an extra session boundary being recorded in the meter.
- The meter increments token counts at two points: after chunk finalize and at session close. In normal flows the chunk finalize is idempotent, but when a reconnect happens the finalize event can replay leading to double-counting for a minority of streaming sessions.
- This is most visible on high-concurrency days and for sessions using the streaming retry knob (client-side immediate reconnect).

Estimated impact for 2026-03-31: ~2.0–2.3M tokens overcounted. I’ve created INF-8421 with logs and a proposed reconciliation script to dedupe finalize events.

Next steps: I can run the dedupe pass for Cloudify’s tenant and produce a corrected token export + a CSV with per-session adjustments. ETA: EOD 2026-04-11.

Marcus Lin
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Internal link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421]

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chen <emma@cloudify.io>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained surge / session-sampling variance on March invoice — proposed reconciliation

Hi Emma — Marcus confirmed a streaming-session finalize replay bug that impacted a small percentage of streaming sessions on 2026-03-31. He ran a dedupe pass and attached a reconciliation file showing the per-session adjustments and the net token credit.

Summary:
- Billed tokens on 2026-03-31: +2,112,430 tokens over Cloudify’s counter for that day.
- Dedupe correction applied: 2,064,210 tokens credited back.
- Remaining delta (~48k tokens) appears to be attributable to timing differences between our bucket boundary and Cloudify’s local aggregation window; we can reconcile that if needed.
- Proposed customer credit: $12,450 (applied to next invoice) — this is the platform credit for the deduped tokens per your signed terms.

I attached the reconciliation CSV and the output of Marcus’ script. Please confirm you accept the credit and that we should apply it to the next invoice, or if you’d prefer a standalone credit note. If you want a brief call to walk through the CSV I’m free tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT.

Attachments: reconciliation_apr10.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
